title: Compact stream snapshots and delegated cred proxy across Py/TS/Go SDKs
author: Sofia Ruiz
commits: introduce compact stream snapshot API and low-overhead cursor (py/ts/go)
implement delegated credential proxy + token exchange helper across SDKs
add unit and integration tests for snapshot/resume semantics
docs: surface migration guide and example in quickstarts
body: Motivation: Several customers and internal teams asked for a low-friction way to resume long-running streaming operations after transient failures or redeploys while minimizing token and CPU overhead. This PR introduces a compact 'snapshot' abstraction for SDK streaming clients and a small delegated credential proxy helper to ensure resumed streams can re-establish auth without exposing raw long-lived secrets. Design goals: (1) minimal runtime overhead for hot paths, (2) language-parity across Python/TypeScript/Go, (3) clear migration story and examples. What this PR does: Adds a lightweight SnapshotCursor object in each SDK that captures just enough state to resume from a server-acknowledged offset (KV-cache position + user-supplied metadata). The cursor is intentionally compact (serializes to a <1KB protobuf/json blob) to make it safe to persist in application caches or use as a checkpoint token. Adds a DelegatedCredProxy utility that wraps token exchange flows: SDKs can call Delegate().WithContext(...) to obtain a short-lived resume token which the server validates before permitting a snapshot resume. This enables customers to persist snapshots without storing long-lived API keys. Cross-language parity: The public API shape was kept consistent across all three SDKs: SnapshotCursor.save(), SnapshotCursor.restore(), DelegatedProxy.exchangeForResumeToken(). All three implementations include identical retry semantics around exchange calls (adaptive backoff profile 'resume-fast' with a short max-retries by default). Ergonomics: default constructors are zero-config so existing users get no behavior change until they opt in. The snapshot APIs also expose a background prefetch hint to allow the runtime to warm KV cache for the resumed sequence (opt-in). Tests & CI: unit tests for snapshot serialization and restore are added in each SDK and there is an end-to-end integration test that runs against a local test harness (invoked in the 'integration' CI job). Documentation: quickstart and migration guide added at docs/quickstarts/stream-checkpointing.md along with a snippet showing how to persist snapshots to Redis and restore after process restart. Checklist: - [x] API implementation in Python/TypeScript/Go - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs + migration guide - [x] version bumps and changelog entries - [x] security review for delegated proxy flow Backwards compatibility: SnapshotCursor is opt-in and does not change default streaming behavior. DelegatedCredProxy introduces a new helper but existing direct-key flows remain supported. Performance: microbenchmarks show <2% median latency increase in hot-path streaming when snapshot hooks are installed (with prefetch disabled). Release notes: see CHANGELOG.md entry.
review_comments: Noah Chen: Can we reduce the default retry attempts for the token exchange? In high-churn environments a long retry window may create token contention.
Sofia Ruiz: Lowered default from 5 -> 3 attempts and added an environment override (REDWOOD_RESUME_RETRY_MAX). Added tests to validate override behavior.
Priya Singh: Please confirm the snapshot serialization format is forward compatible (fields can be ignored by older clients).
Sofia Ruiz: SnapshotCursor uses a versioned wrapper and includes a stable 'version' field. Added a migration note in docs and a unit test for unknown-field tolerance.
Marco Alvarez: Security review note: ensure resume tokens are single-use or time-limited. Also recommend recording a resume audit event.

Sofia Ruiz: DelegatedCredProxy issues time-limited tokens (default TTL 5m) and additionally a single-use flag can be toggled. The server-side audit hook was coordinated with infra and tagged in SUP-7421.
ci_checks: test: py unit & ts unit & go unit ✓
release_notes: Added compact SnapshotCursor and DelegatedCredProxy across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Snapshots enable resumable streaming with a small persisted token; DelegatedCredProxy enables safe resume without persisting long-lived API keys. Opt-in feature; default behavior unchanged. SDK versions bumped: python -> 1.9.0, typescript -> 2.6.3, go -> 1.5.1.
notes: Small compatibility follow-up scheduled: add server-side TTL override and exposable telemetry tag for resumed streams (ENG-1463).
